CHIEF COMPLAINT
Difficulty with asthma during sports and concerns about mood.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Patient is a student who reports dealing with asthma and attempted to join sports, specifically water polo. Reports difficulty breathing during matches, requiring stopping activity and sitting on the sideline to catch breath and use inhaler. Describes symptoms as phlegm building up in throat, coughing, chest tightness, and wheezing with associated lightheadedness. Uses albuterol inhaler (two puffs) for symptoms, which alleviates the problem but requires patient to sit down. Notes shakiness as side effect of inhaler. Symptoms occur pretty much every time patient does aerobic workouts. Also notes coughing when around smoke but typically avoids these situations. Denies nighttime symptoms. Currently only uses albuterol inhaler during attacks, not on any daily asthma medications. Additionally reports mood concerns, feeling stressed due to SAT studying and AP classes. Describes feeling down, lack of motivation, friends wanting to go out but patient prefers to stay home, and reports being really tired a lot. Patient states these mood changes started this year.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Reports seasonal allergies. Denies nighttime asthma symptoms. No other systems reviewed.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Asthma.

MEDICATIONS
Albuterol inhaler (two puffs as needed for symptoms).

ALLERGIES
Not discussed.

FAMILY HISTORY
Not discussed.

SOCIAL HISTORY
Patient is a student studying for SATs and taking AP classes. Interested in sports, particularly water polo. Lives with friends who invite patient out socially.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Heart and lungs: Normal. Eyes: Normal. Ears: Small amount of fluid noted bilaterally. Mouth and throat: Fine, no tonsils. Abdomen: Normal bowel sounds, palpation normal. Reflexes: Normal.

RESULTS
Not discussed.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
1. Asthma: Patient presenting with exercise-induced asthma symptoms. Will start daily montelukast (Singulair) for asthma control, which may also help with possible allergic component. Continue albuterol inhaler as needed. Counseled that shakiness is expected side effect; recommend sitting down after use. Patient to return in six weeks for follow-up; should see improvement within about one month.
2. Mood: Symptoms consistent with stress related to school expectations and upcoming exams. Recommend starting therapy. Screening questionnaires to be completed. Follow-up in a couple of weeks.
